issue.title: test_update_shortcut_dispatch_performs_no_disk_or_subprocess_work fails cold: patches Path.read_text before the keymap defaults cache is warm
issue.description:
Proposed by the sase-1qt landing tale coder (sase-1qt.land--code, 2026-11-01; recorded in sase-1qt epic note #3 LIMITS) and triaged by the relaunched sase-1qt land agent on 2026-11-02. Not caused by sase-1qt.

`tests/ace/tui/test_log_panel_keymap.py::test_update_shortcut_dispatch_performs_no_disk_or_subprocess_work` fails when it runs cold in a fresh process (for example alone, or first on an xdist worker). It monkeypatches `Path.read_text`, `Path.write_text`, `subprocess.run`/`Popen` and the update/agents-sync status getters to raise, then calls `action_update_sase_shortcut()`. In a cold process, the keymap defaults cache has not been populated yet, so dispatch reads keymap defaults from disk through the patched `Path.read_text` and the test fails. Inside the broader suite another test warms the cache first, so it passes. The coder verified the identical failure on the unmodified tree (sase `d26baecb05`), so it predates the epic's edits.

Likely fix (test isolation, keep the assertion): warm the keymap defaults and any other load-once config the dispatch path legitimately needs before installing the patches, or give the test an explicit warmed fixture. The test's real claim is that keypress dispatch performs no disk or subprocess work after startup; it should not depend on another test having warmed the cache. Check whether dispatch reads anything per keypress (that would be a real product bug).

Related: the epic sase-j7 class (process-global state shared between tests). This is the inverse shape: a hidden dependency on a warm global cache, not a leak. Not routed there because j7's scope is leak detection and mechanism fixes for leaking state.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic: fails every time it runs cold in isolation (verified on the unmodified tree at d26baecb05 by the sase-1qt tale coder), and passes only when an earlier test in the same process has warmed the keymap defaults cache.

issue.creation_reason: The sase-1qt landing tale found this order-dependent failure while verifying unrelated repairs, and it was never filed because that run's work was lost; a test that fails whenever it runs first in a process is a latent lane failure.
